text: Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS complying with the definition of paragraph 2.1 shall, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, meet the performance requirements of paragraphs 5.1 and 5.3 to 5.6 of this Regulation.
condition: all vehicles, when the AEBS is activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges

text: Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS submitted to approval for the vehicle to vehicle scenario shall, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, meet the performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.1.
condition: vehicles submitted to approval for vehicle to vehicle scenario

text: Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS submitted to approval for the vehicle to pedestrian scenario shall, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, meet the performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.2.
condition: vehicles submitted to approval for vehicle to pedestrian scenario

text: The effectiveness of the AEBS shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields.
The immunity of the AEBS to magnetic or electrical fields shall be demonstrated by compliance with the 05 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
Conformity of the AEBS with the safety aspects of electronic control systems shall be shown by meeting the requirements of Annex 3.
In addition to the collision warnings, the AEBS shall provide the driver with the appropriate warnings specified in paragraphs 5.1.4.1 to 5.1.4.3.
The AEBS shall provide the driver with a failure warning when there is a failure in the AEBS that prevents the requirements of this Regulation from being met.
condition: when there is a failure in the AEBS that prevents the requirements of this Regulation from being met

text: The AEBS failure warning shall be as specified in paragraph 5.5.4 (constant yellow optical warning signal).
There shall not be an appreciable time interval between each AEBS self-check.
There shall not be a delay in illuminating the AEBS failure warning signal in the case of an electrically detectable failure.
condition: in the case of an electrically detectable failure

text: Upon detection of any non-electrical failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment), the AEBS failure warning signal as defined in paragraph 5.1.4.1 shall be illuminated.
condition: upon detection of any non-electrical failure condition

text: If the AEBS has not been initialised after a cumulative driving time of 15 seconds above a speed of 10 km/h, information of this status shall be indicated to the driver.
condition: if the system has not been initialised after a cumulative driving time of 15 seconds above 10 km/h

text: The information that the AEBS has not been initialised shall exist until the system has been successfully initialised.
A deactivation warning shall be given when the AEBS is deactivated, as specified in paragraph 5.4.4.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a means to deactivate the AEBS

text: Subject to the provisions of paragraphs 5.3.1 and 5.3.2, the AEBS shall provide emergency braking interventions described in paragraphs 5.2.1.2 and 5.2.2.2 having the purpose of significantly decreasing the speed of the subject vehicle.
condition: subject to driver interruption provisions of paragraphs 5.3.1 and 5.3.2

text: The AEBS shall be designed to minimise the generation of collision warning signals in situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision.
condition: situations with no risk of an imminent collision

text: The AEBS shall be designed to avoid advanced emergency braking in situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision.
condition: situations with no risk of an imminent collision

text: False reaction avoidance shall be demonstrated in the assessment carried out under Annex 3, and this assessment shall include in particular the scenarios listed in Appendix 2 of Annex 3.
Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS shall meet the performance requirements of UN Regulation No. 13 in its 11 series of amendments for vehicles of Category M2, M3, N2, N3.
Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS shall be equipped with an anti-lock system in accordance with the performance requirements of Annex 13 to UN Regulation No. 13 in its 11 series of amendments.

Where the deceleration is limited in empty load conditions and this is demonstrated by the manufacturer to the technical service, the mass-in-running-order requirements of the tables in paragraphs 5.2.1.4 and 5.2.2.4 shall be deemed fulfilled if the impact speed requirements are met with an added mass on the rear axle calculated to implement an α value between 1.3 and 1.5, with α = Wr/W × L/H (Wr rear axle load, W subject vehicle mass, L wheelbase, H centre of gravity height in running order).
condition: deceleration limited in empty load conditions, demonstrated by the manufacturer to the technical service

text: When the added rear axle mass alternative is used, the relative impact speed shall additionally be measured with the vehicle mass in running order and the result appended to the test report.
condition: when the added rear axle mass alternative of paragraph 5.1.8 is used

text: When the added rear axle mass alternative is used, the vehicle shall reach a relative avoidance speed reduced by α/1.3 when in configuration of mass in running order.
condition: when the added rear axle mass alternative of paragraph 5.1.8 is used

text: When an imminent collision with a preceding vehicle of Category M, N or O is detected in the same lane with a relative speed above that up to which the subject vehicle is able to avoid the collision (within the conditions of paragraph 5.2.1.4), a collision warning as specified in paragraph 5.5.1 shall be provided.
condition: vehicle to vehicle scenario; relative speed above the collision avoidance speed

text: The vehicle to vehicle collision warning shall be triggered at the latest 0.8 seconds before the start of emergency braking.
condition: vehicle to vehicle scenario

text: In case the collision cannot be anticipated in time to give a collision warning 0.8 seconds ahead of emergency braking, a collision warning as specified in paragraph 5.5.1 shall be provided no later than the start of the emergency braking.
condition: vehicle to vehicle scenario; collision cannot be anticipated in time for 0.8 s warning

text: The vehicle to vehicle collision warning may be aborted only if the conditions prevailing a collision are no longer present.
condition: vehicle to vehicle scenario

text: The vehicle to vehicle collision warning performance shall be verified according to paragraphs 6.4 and 6.5.
condition: vehicle to vehicle scenario

text: When the AEBS has detected the possibility of an imminent collision with a preceding vehicle, there shall be a braking demand of at least 4 m/s² to the service braking system of the vehicle.
condition: vehicle to vehicle scenario

text: Deceleration demand values higher than 4 m/s² during the collision warning are permitted only for very short durations (e.g. as haptic warning).
condition: vehicle to vehicle scenario, during collision warning phase

text: The emergency braking may be aborted, or the deceleration demand reduced below 4 m/s², only if the conditions prevailing a collision are no longer present or the risk of a collision has decreased.
condition: vehicle to vehicle scenario

text: The vehicle to vehicle emergency braking performance shall be verified according to paragraphs 6.4 and 6.5.
condition: vehicle to vehicle scenario

text: The AEBS (vehicle to vehicle) shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 10 km/h and the maximum design speed of the vehicle and at all vehicle load conditions, unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.

text: In absence of driver input leading to interruption according to paragraph 5.3.2, the AEBS shall be able to achieve a relative impact speed less than or equal to the maximum relative impact speed of Table 1, provided the conditions (a) to (d) of paragraph 5.2.1.4 (road, weather, vehicle state, sensing, unambiguous situation) are fulfilled.

text: The AEBS shall provide appropriate and robust means for the driver to interrupt the collision warning.
The AEBS shall provide appropriate and robust means for the driver to interrupt the emergency braking.

Interruption of the collision warning or emergency braking may be initiated only by a positive action (e.g. kick-down or a swerving action resulting in enough change of direction to not hit the target) that indicates that the driver is aware of the emergency situation.
The vehicle manufacturer shall provide a list of the driver positive actions that interrupt the AEBS to the technical service at the time of type approval, and it shall be annexed to the test report.

The AEBS function shall be automatically reinstated at each initiation of the powertrain; an automatically performed new engine start (e.g. stop/start system) shall not be considered an initiation of the powertrain.
condition: vehicle equipped with a means to manually deactivate the AEBS

text: The AEBS deactivation control shall be designed in such a way that manual deactivation shall not be possible with less than two deliberate actions.
condition: vehicle equipped with a means to manually deactivate the AEBS

text: The location of the AEBS deactivation control shall comply with the relevant requirements and transitional provisions of UN Regulation No. 121 in its 01 series of amendments or any later series of amendments.
condition: vehicle equipped with a means to manually deactivate the AEBS

text: For every manual deactivation requested by the driver, the AEBS shall be automatically reinstated at the latest after 15 minutes.
condition: vehicle equipped with a means to manually deactivate the AEBS

text: It shall be possible for the driver to reactivate the AEBS at any time, including whilst driving.
condition: vehicle equipped with a means to manually deactivate the AEBS

text: The AEBS may provide a technical means for the driver to deactivate the system following a unique procedure only in case of a situation impairing the operation of the system (e.g. sensor mounting damage by an accident).
condition: if a driver unique-procedure deactivation means is provided

text: The manufacturer shall provide information about the situations permitting the unique-procedure deactivation in the vehicle owner's handbook or by any other communication means in the vehicle.
condition: if a driver unique-procedure deactivation means is provided

text: The unique deactivation procedure shall be possible only while the vehicle is at standstill for a minimum time duration of 2 minutes with the master control switch active.
condition: if a driver unique-procedure deactivation means is provided

text: The unique deactivation procedure shall require a more complex procedure than the manual deactivation of paragraph 5.4.1.2 (e.g. at least three different deliberate actions).
condition: if a driver unique-procedure deactivation means is provided

text: The vehicle manufacturer shall provide a list of situations and corresponding criteria where the AEBS function is automatically deactivated to the technical service at the time of type approval, and it shall be annexed to the test report.
condition: vehicle equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the AEBS

text: The AEBS function shall be automatically reactivated as soon as the conditions that led to the automatic deactivation are not present anymore.
condition: vehicle equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the AEBS

text: Where automatic deactivation of the AEBS is a consequence of the driver manually switching off the vehicle stability function, this deactivation shall require at least two deliberate actions by the driver.
condition: automatic AEBS deactivation caused by driver switching off the vehicle stability function

text: The AEBS may provide a technical means to deactivate the system only for specific applications (e.g. front mounted equipment like snow plough) where the operation of the system may be impaired.
condition: specific applications where operation of the system may be impaired

text: The technical means to deactivate the AEBS for specific applications shall not be made available to the driver (e.g. only possible with a unique operation by an authorized workshop).
condition: if a workshop deactivation means for specific applications is provided

text: For AEBS deactivated by the workshop technical means, the deactivation warning of paragraph 5.1.4.3 may be suppressed only at the earliest 15 seconds after the initiation of each new ignition cycle.
condition: AEBS deactivated by workshop technical means for specific applications

text: A constant optical warning signal shall inform the driver that the AEBS function has been deactivated; the yellow warning signal of paragraph 5.5.4 may be used for this purpose.
condition: when the AEBS function has been deactivated

text: While automated driving functions are in longitudinal control of the vehicle (e.g. ALKS active), the AEBS function may be suspended or its control strategies adapted without indication to the driver only as long as it remains ensured that the vehicle provides at least the same collision avoidance capabilities as the AEBS function during manual operation.
condition: while automated driving functions are in longitudinal control of the vehicle

text: The collision warning referred to in paragraphs 5.2.1.1. and 5.2.2.1. shall be provided by at least two modes selected from acoustic, haptic or optical.

A description of the warning indication and the sequence in which the collision warning signals are presented to the driver shall be provided by the vehicle manufacturer at the time of type-approval and recorded in the test report.
Where an optical means is used as part of the collision warning, the optical signal may be the flashing of the failure warning signal specified in paragraph 5.5.4.
condition: where an optical means is used as part of the collision warning

text: The AEBS failure warning referred to in paragraph 5.1.4.1. shall be a constant yellow optical warning signal.

Each AEBS optical warning signal shall be activated either when the ignition (start) switch is turned to the "on" (run) position or when the ignition (start) switch is in a position between the "on" (run) and "start" position that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position (initial system (power-on)).
condition: does not apply to warning signals shown in a common space

text: The AEBS optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight.
The satisfactory condition of the AEBS optical warning signals must be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.
When the driver is provided with an optical warning signal to indicate that the AEBS is temporarily not available (e.g. due to inclement weather conditions), the signal shall be constant.
condition: when an optical signal indicates the AEBS is temporarily not available

text: The failure warning signal specified in paragraph 5.5.4. may be used to indicate that the AEBS is temporarily not available.
condition: when an optical signal indicates the AEBS is temporarily not available

text: At a Periodic Technical Inspection, it shall be possible to confirm the correct operational status of the AEBS by a visible observation of the failure warning signal status following a "power-ON" and any bulb check.
Where the failure warning signal is in a common space, the common space must be observed to be functional prior to the failure warning signal status check.
condition: if the failure warning signal is in a common space

text: At the time of type approval, the means chosen by the manufacturer to protect against simple unauthorised modification of the operation of the failure warning signal shall be confidentially outlined; alternatively this is fulfilled when a secondary means of checking the correct operational status of the AEBS is available.
The test shall be performed on a flat, dry, concrete or asphalt road affording good adhesion.
The test surface shall have a consistent slope between level and 1 per cent.
The ambient temperature during testing shall be between 0°C and 45°C.
The horizontal visibility range shall allow the target to be observed throughout the test.
The tests shall be performed when there is no wind liable to affect the results.
Natural ambient illumination must be homogeneous in the test area and in excess of 1000 lux for the vehicle to vehicle scenario.
condition: vehicle to vehicle scenario

text: Natural ambient illumination must be homogeneous in the test area and in excess of 2000 lux for the vehicle to pedestrian scenario.
condition: vehicle to pedestrian scenario

text: Tests may be conducted under deviating test conditions (e.g. not dry surface, below the minimum ambient temperature, non-articulated pedestrian target) only at the request of the manufacturer and with the agreement of the Technical Service, and the performance requirements shall still be met.
condition: at the request of the manufacturer and with agreement of the Technical Service

text: The vehicle shall be tested at the maximum mass.

If deemed justified, the technical service may test at the mass in running order with an additional mass of maximum 125 kg including measuring equipment and a possible second person, to demonstrate compliance with the requirements referring to mass in running order.
condition: if deemed justified by the technical service

text: The test load distribution shall be according to the manufacturer's recommendation and be annexed to the test report.
No alteration of the vehicle load shall be made once the test procedure has begun.
During the series of test runs, the fuel level may decrease but shall never fall below 50 per cent.

If requested by the vehicle manufacturer, the vehicle can be driven a maximum of 100 km on a mixture of urban and rural roads with other traffic and roadside furniture to initialise the sensor system.
condition: if requested by the vehicle manufacturer

text: If requested by the vehicle manufacturer, the vehicle can undergo a sequence of brake activations to ensure the service brake system is bedded in prior to the test.
condition: if requested by the vehicle manufacturer

text: If requested by the vehicle manufacturer, the average temperature of the service brakes on the hottest axle, measured inside the brake linings or on the braking path of the disc or drum, is below 100°C prior to each test run.
condition: if requested by the vehicle manufacturer

text: Details of the pre-test condition strategy requested by the vehicle manufacturer shall be identified and recorded in the vehicle type approval documentation.
The mounted tyres shall be identified and recorded in the vehicle type approval documentation.
The vehicle may be fitted with protective equipment only if it does not affect the results of the tests.
condition: if protective equipment is fitted

text: The target used for the vehicle detection tests shall be a regular high-volume series production passenger car of Category M1 or alternatively a soft target representative of a passenger vehicle in terms of its identification characteristics applicable to the AEBS sensor system according to ISO 19206-3:2021.
The reference point for the location of the target vehicle shall be the most rearward point on the centreline of the vehicle.
The target used for the pedestrian detection tests shall be a child articulated soft target representative of the human attributes applicable to the AEBS sensor system according to ISO 19206-2:2018.

In the stationary vehicle target test, the subject vehicle shall approach the stationary target in a straight line for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test with a subject vehicle to target centreline offset of not more than 0.2 m.
Stationary vehicle target tests shall be conducted at a subject vehicle speed of 20 km/h with a tolerance of +/- 2 km/h, not beyond the range specified in paragraph 5.2.1.3.

Stationary vehicle target tests shall be conducted at the maximum required impact avoidance speed as shown in paragraph 5.2.1.4., with a tolerance of +/- 2 km/h, not beyond the range specified in paragraph 5.2.1.3.

Stationary vehicle target tests shall be conducted at the maximum required impact avoidance speed as shown in paragraph 5.2.1.4. + 8 km/h, or the maximum design speed, whichever is lower, with a tolerance of +/- 2 km/h.

If deemed justified, the technical service may test in any test condition within paragraph 5.2.1.4., with any other speeds listed in the tables of paragraph 5.2.1.4. and within the speed range of paragraph 5.2.1.3.
condition: if deemed justified by the technical service

text: Where the Technical Service verifies that the control strategy is not unreasonably changed or AEBS switched off in conditions other than those of paragraph 5.2.1.4., the report of this verification shall be appended to the test report.
condition: if such verification is performed

text: The functional part of the stationary vehicle target test shall start with the subject vehicle travelling at the required test speed within the tolerances and lateral offset prescribed, and at a distance corresponding to a TTC of at least 4 seconds from the target.
The tolerances shall be respected between the start of the functional part of the stationary vehicle target test and the system intervention.

In the moving vehicle target test, the subject vehicle and the moving target shall travel in a straight line, in the same direction, for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test with a subject vehicle to target centreline offset of not more than 0.2 m.

In the moving vehicle target test, the target shall travel at 20 km/h with a tolerance of +0/-2 km/h for both the target and the subject vehicle, and relative speeds shall have a tolerance of +/- 2 km/h, at speeds not beyond the range specified in paragraph 5.2.1.3.
Moving vehicle target tests shall be conducted at a relative speed of 20 km/h to the target.
Moving vehicle target tests shall be conducted at a relative speed equal to the maximum required impact avoidance speed as shown in paragraph 5.2.1.4.

Moving vehicle target tests shall be conducted at a relative speed equal to the maximum required impact avoidance speed of paragraph 5.2.1.4. + 8 km/h, or at the maximum design speed, whichever is lower.

If deemed justified, the technical service may test in any test condition within paragraph 5.2.1.4., with any other speeds listed in the tables of paragraph 5.2.1.4. and within the speed range of paragraph 5.2.1.3.
condition: if deemed justified by the technical service

text: Where the Technical Service verifies, outside the conditions of paragraph 5.2.1.4., that the control strategy is not unreasonably changed or AEBS switched off, the report of this verification shall be appended to the test report.
condition: if such verification is performed

text: The functional part of the moving vehicle target test shall start with the subject vehicle at the required test speed within tolerances and lateral offset, the moving target at the required test speed within tolerances, and a distance corresponding to a TTC of at least 4 seconds from the target.
The tolerances shall be respected between the start of the functional part of the moving vehicle target test and the system intervention.

In the pedestrian target test, the subject vehicle shall approach the impact point in a straight line for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test with an anticipated subject vehicle to impact point centreline offset of not more than 0.2 m.

The functional part of the pedestrian target test shall start when the subject vehicle is travelling at a constant speed at a distance corresponding to a TTC of at least 4 seconds from the collision point.

The pedestrian target shall travel in a straight line perpendicular to the subject vehicle's direction of travel at a constant speed of 5 km/h +0/-0.4 km/h, starting not before the functional part of the test has started.

The pedestrian target's positioning shall be coordinated so that the impact point on the front of the subject vehicle is on the vehicle's longitudinal centreline with a tolerance of not more than 0.1 m, if the subject vehicle remained at the test speed without braking.
Pedestrian target tests shall be conducted at a subject vehicle speed of 20 km/h with a tolerance of +/- 2 km/h, not beyond the range specified in paragraph 5.2.2.3.
Pedestrian target tests shall be conducted at the maximum required collision avoidance speed with a tolerance of +/- 2 km/h.

Pedestrian target tests shall be conducted at the maximum required impact avoidance speed of paragraph 5.2.2.4. + 8 km/h, or the maximum design speed, whichever is lower, with a tolerance of +/- 2 km/h.

If deemed justified, the technical service may test in any test condition within paragraph 5.2.2.4., with any other speeds listed in the table of paragraph 5.2.2.4. and within the speed range of paragraph 5.2.2.3.
condition: if deemed justified by the technical service

text: Where the Technical Service verifies, outside the conditions of paragraph 5.2.2.4., that the control strategy is not unreasonably changed or AEBS switched off, the report of this verification shall be appended to the test report.
condition: if such verification is performed

text: The functional part of the pedestrian target test shall start with the subject vehicle at the required test speed within tolerances and lateral offset, the pedestrian target at the required speed within tolerances, and a distance corresponding to a TTC of at least 4 seconds from the target; tolerances shall be respected until system intervention.
The pedestrian test shall be carried out with a child pedestrian soft target defined in 6.3.2.

The assessment of the impact speed shall be based on the actual contact point between the target and the vehicle, taking into account the actual vehicle shape without additional protective equipment permitted per paragraph 6.2.4.
For the failure detection test, an electrical failure shall be simulated, e.g. by disconnecting the power source to any AEBS component or any electrical connection between AEBS components.

When simulating an AEBS failure, neither the electrical connections for the driver failure warning signal of paragraph 5.5.4. nor the optional manual AEBS deactivation control of paragraph 5.4.1. shall be disconnected.
With a simulated failure, the failure warning signal shall be activated and remain activated not later than 10 s after the vehicle has been driven at a speed greater than 10 km/h.
condition: as long as the simulated failure exists

text: The failure warning signal shall be reactivated immediately after a subsequent ignition "off" ignition "on" cycle with the vehicle stationary as long as the simulated failure exists.
condition: as long as the simulated failure exists

text: When the AEBS is manually deactivated with the ignition switch in the "on" (run) position, the deactivation warning signal of paragraph 5.4.4. shall be activated.
condition: vehicles equipped with means to manually deactivate the AEBS

text: After turning the ignition switch to "off" and again to "on" (run), the previously activated deactivation warning signal shall not be reactivated, indicating that the AEBS has been reinstated as specified in paragraph 5.4.1.
condition: vehicles equipped with means to manually deactivate the AEBS

text: If the ignition system is activated by means of a key, the deactivation test requirement shall be fulfilled without removing the key.
condition: if the ignition system is activated by a key

text: Each test scenario (one test setup at one subject vehicle speed at one load condition of one category) shall be performed two times; if one of the two runs fails, the test may be repeated once, and the scenario is passed if the required performance is met in two test runs.
The number of failed test runs shall not exceed 10.0 per cent of the performed test runs for the Vehicle to Vehicle tests.
The number of failed test runs shall not exceed 10.0 per cent of the performed test runs for the Vehicle to Pedestrian tests.

If the total number of test runs within a category would be less than 10, additional test runs of that category may be performed, including but not limited to the failed scenario, to reach at least 10 test runs.
condition: if total test runs within a category are less than 10

text: The root cause of any failed test run shall be analysed together with the Technical Service and annexed to the test report.

If the root cause of a failed test run cannot be linked to a deviation in the test setup, the Technical Service may test at any other speed within the speed range defined in paragraphs 5.2.1.3., 5.2.1.4., 5.2.2.3. or 5.2.2.4. as relevant.
condition: if the root cause is not linked to a test setup deviation

text: During the Annex 3 assessment, the manufacturer shall demonstrate via appropriate documentation that the system is capable of reliably delivering the required performances.

For the false reaction test, two stationary M1 vehicles (or passenger-vehicle soft targets according to ISO 19206-3:2021) shall be positioned facing the same direction of travel as the subject vehicle, 4.5 m apart, with their rears aligned.
In the false reaction test, the subject vehicle shall travel for at least 60 m at a constant speed of 50 ± 2 km/h to pass centrally between the two stationary vehicles.
During the false reaction test there shall be no adjustment of any subject vehicle control other than slight steering adjustments to counteract drifting.
In the false reaction test, the AEBS shall not provide a collision warning.
In the false reaction test, the AEBS shall not initiate the emergency braking phase.
Virtual testing used at the request of the vehicle manufacturer as an alternative for tests of paragraphs 6.4. to 6.6. shall be verified, validated and used in accordance with Annex 4.
condition: if virtual testing is used

text: Virtual testing may be used in the evaluation of the warning and activation tests in accordance with paragraph 1.8. of Schedule 3 and Schedule 8 of Revision 3 of the 1958 Agreement.
condition: if virtual testing is used

text: Where virtual testing is used, at least 30 per cent of required tests shall be performed physically, including at least one test of each scenario variant of paragraphs 6.4 to 6.6 relevant for the approval.
condition: if virtual testing is used

text: The physical tests to be performed shall be agreed between the manufacturer and the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service; tests performed for model validation corresponding to the type approval can count towards the 30 per cent.
condition: if virtual testing is used

text: In the case of modification of the vehicle type and extension of approval, the proportion of physical tests may be less than 30 per cent of required tests and shall be agreed between the manufacturer and the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service.
condition: in case of modification and extension of approval

text: Where virtual testing is used by the manufacturer, a separate report including at least the additional information specified in Annex 4 shall be annexed to the test report.
condition: if virtual testing is used

text: Procedures concerning conformity of production shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
A vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements of paragraph 5.

The Type Approval Authority which granted approval may at any time verify the conformity of control methods applicable to each production unit; the normal frequency of such inspections shall be once every two years.
The approval mark affixed to the vehicle shall have the dimension a of at least 8 mm.
The approval mark shall be marked with C for Vehicle to Vehicle and P for Vehicle to Pedestrian approval scenarios.
The requirements of Annex 3 shall also apply to safety related functions identified in this Regulation which are controlled by electronic system(s).

The information disclosed to the Technical Service shall show that "The System" respects, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in this Regulation.
The information disclosed to the Technical Service shall show that "The System" is designed to operate in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.

The manufacturer shall provide a documentation package which gives access to the basic design of "The System" and the means by which it is linked to other vehicle systems or by which it directly controls output variables.
The function(s) of "The System" and the safety concept, as laid down by the manufacturer, shall be explained in the documentation.
The documentation shall be brief, yet provide evidence that the design and development has had the benefit of expertise from all the system fields which are involved.
For periodic technical inspections, the documentation shall describe how the current operational status of "The System" can be checked.

The Technical Service shall assess the documentation package to show that "The System" is designed to operate, under non-fault and fault conditions, in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.

The Technical Service shall assess the documentation package to show that "The System" respects, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in this Regulation.
The Technical Service shall assess the documentation package to show that "The System" was developed according to the development process/method declared by the manufacturer.

The formal documentation package for the approval, containing the material listed in paragraph 3 of Annex 3 (except that of paragraph 3.4.4), shall be supplied to the Technical Service at the time of submission of the type approval application.
The formal documentation package shall be used by the Technical Service as the basic reference for the verification process set out in paragraph 4 of Annex 3.

The Technical Service shall ensure that the formal documentation package remains available for a period determined in agreement with the Approval Authority, of at least 10 years counted from the time when production of the vehicle is definitely discontinued.
Additional material and analysis data of paragraph 3.4.4 shall be retained by the manufacturer but made open for inspection at the time of type approval.

The manufacturer shall ensure that the additional material and analysis data remains available for a period of 10 years counted from the time when production of the vehicle is definitely discontinued.

A description shall be provided which gives a simple explanation of all the control functions of "The System" and the methods employed to achieve the objectives, including a statement of the mechanism(s) by which control is exercised.
Any described function of "The System" that can be over-ridden shall be identified and a further description of the changed rationale of the function's operation provided.
condition: if a described function can be over-ridden

text: A list of all input and sensed variables of "The System" shall be provided and the working range of these defined.
A list of all output variables which are controlled by "The System" shall be provided, with an indication in each case of whether the control is direct or via another vehicle system.
The range of control exercised by "The System" on each output variable shall be defined.
Limits defining the boundaries of functional operation of "The System" shall be stated where appropriate to system performance.
condition: where appropriate to system performance

text: A list shall be provided collating all the units of "The System" and mentioning the other vehicle systems which are needed to achieve the control function in question.
An outline schematic showing the units of "The System" in combination shall be provided with both the equipment distribution and the interconnections made clear.
The function of each unit of "The System" shall be outlined and the signals linking it with other units or with other vehicle systems shall be shown.

Interconnections within "The System" shall be shown by a circuit diagram for the electric transmission links, by a piping diagram for pneumatic or hydraulic transmission equipment and by a simplified diagrammatic layout for mechanical linkages.
The transmission links both to and from other systems shall also be shown.
There shall be a clear correspondence between the transmission links and the signals and/or operating data carried between units of "The System".
Priorities of signals and/or operating data on multiplexed data paths shall be stated wherever priority may be an issue affecting performance or safety as far as this Regulation is concerned.
condition: wherever priority may affect performance or safety

text: Each unit of "The System" shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable (e.g. by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content) to provide corresponding hardware and documentation association.
Where functions are combined within a single unit or single computer but shown in multiple blocks in the block diagram, only a single hardware identification marking shall be used.
condition: where functions are combined within a single unit or computer

text: The manufacturer shall, by the use of the unit identification, affirm that the equipment supplied conforms to the corresponding document.

The unit identification shall define the hardware and software version and shall be changed where the software changes such as to alter the function of the unit as far as this Regulation is concerned.
condition: where the software changes so as to alter the function of the unit

text: The manufacturer shall provide a statement which affirms that the strategy chosen to achieve "The System" objectives will not, under non-fault conditions, prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle.
In respect of software employed in "The System", the outline architecture shall be explained and the design methods and tools used shall be identified.
The manufacturer shall show evidence of the means by which they determined the realisation of the system logic during the design and development process.
The manufacturer shall provide the Technical Service with an explanation of the design provisions built into "The System" so as to generate safe operation under fault conditions.
In case of a failure in "The System", the driver shall be warned, for example by warning signal or message display.
condition: in case of a failure

text: The failure warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists, when the system is not deactivated by the driver.
condition: when the system is not deactivated by the driver

text: If the chosen provision selects a partial performance mode of operation under certain fault conditions, these conditions shall be stated and the resulting limits of effectiveness defined.
condition: if a partial performance mode is selected under fault conditions

text: If the chosen provision selects a second (back-up) means to realise the vehicle control system objective, the principles of the change-over mechanism, the logic and level of redundancy and any built-in back-up checking features shall be explained and the resulting limits of back-up effectiveness defined.
condition: if a back-up means is selected

text: If the chosen provision selects the removal of the Higher Level Function, all the corresponding output control signals associated with this function shall be inhibited in such a manner as to limit the transition disturbance.
condition: if removal of the Higher Level Function is selected

text: The documentation shall be supported by an analysis which shows, in overall terms, how the system will behave on the occurrence of any individual hazard or fault which will have a bearing on vehicle control performance or safety.
The chosen analytical approach(es) shall be established and maintained by the manufacturer and made open for inspection by the Technical Service at the time of type approval.
The Technical Service shall perform an assessment of the application of the analytical approach(es).

The audit shall include inspection of the safety approach at the concept (vehicle) level, confirming that it includes consideration of interactions with other vehicle systems, based on a Hazard / Risk analysis appropriate to system safety.

The audit shall include inspection of the safety approach at the system level, based on a Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA), a Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) or any similar process appropriate to system safety.

The audit shall include inspection of the validation plans and results, the validation using for example Hardware in the Loop (HIL) testing, vehicle on-road operational testing, or any means appropriate for validation.

The assessment shall consist of checks of hazards and faults chosen by the Technical Service to establish that the manufacturer's explanation of the safety concept is understandable, logical and that the validation plans are suitable and have been completed.
The documentation shall itemize the parameters being monitored and set out, for each fault condition, the warning signal to be given to the driver and/or to service/technical inspection personnel.

The documentation shall describe the measures in place to ensure "The System" does not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when its performance is affected by environmental conditions, e.g. climatic, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress, ice packing.
The functional operation of "The System", as laid out in the documents required in paragraph 3 of Annex 3, shall be tested as specified in paragraph 4.1 of Annex 3.
The Technical Service shall verify "The System" under non-fault conditions by testing a number of selected functions from those declared by the manufacturer in paragraph 3.2 of Annex 3.
For complex electronic systems, the verification tests shall include scenarios whereby a declared function is overridden.
condition: for complex electronic systems

text: The reaction of "The System" shall be checked under the influence of a failure in any individual unit by applying corresponding output signals to electrical units or mechanical elements in order to simulate the effects of internal faults within the unit.
The Technical Service shall conduct the safety concept check for at least one individual unit, but shall not check the reaction of "The System" to multiple simultaneous failures of individual units.
The Technical Service shall verify that the safety concept tests include aspects that may have an impact on vehicle controllability and user information (HMI aspects).
The verification results shall correspond with the documented summary of the failure analysis, to a level of overall effect such that the safety concept and execution are confirmed as being adequate.

Reporting of the assessment by the Technical Service shall be performed in such a manner that allows traceability, e.g. versions of documents inspected are coded and listed in the records of the Technical Service.

The model assessment form for electronic systems shall be signed by different persons even when the Technical Service and Type Approval Authority are the same, or alternatively a separate Type Approval Authority authorization shall be issued with the report.
condition: when the Technical Service and Type Approval Authority are the same

text: The false reaction scenarios of Appendix 2 to Annex 3 shall be used to assess the AEBS strategies implemented in order to minimize the generation of false reactions.
For each type of false reaction scenario, the vehicle manufacturer shall explain the principle strategies implemented to ensure safety.
The manufacturer shall provide evidence (e.g. simulation results, real-world test data, track test data) of the AEBS behaviour in the described types of false reaction scenarios.

The parameters described in subparagraph 2 of each false reaction scenario shall be used as guidance if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary; until proper values for heavy vehicles are defined, the values may be changed in agreement between the Technical Service and the manufacturer.
condition: if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary

text: False reaction Scenario 1 (left turn or right turn at the intersection) is only applicable to vehicles of Category M2, M3 ≤ 8t and N2 ≤ 8t.
condition: M3 and N2 with maximum mass ≤ 8t

text: In false reaction Scenario 1 (guidance), the subject vehicle drives at 30 km/h (+0/-2 km/h) toward the intersection, decelerates by braking to not less than 16 km/h at the point where it begins to steer left/right with a TTC to the oncoming vehicle of not more than 2.8 seconds, turns at not less than 10 km/h at constant speed, and the TTC to the oncoming vehicle is not more than 1.7 seconds when the overlap ratio becomes 0 per cent.
condition: if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary; M3 and N2 ≤ 8t

text: In false reaction Scenario 2 (guidance), the forward vehicle and subject vehicle drive at 40 km/h (+0/-2 km/h) on a straight road; the forward vehicle decelerates to 10 km/h (+0/-2 km/h) to turn; when the forward vehicle begins to turn the subject vehicle speed is not less than 26 km/h and TTC not more than 4.7 seconds; the subject vehicle then decelerates to not less than 20 km/h at constant speed and the TTC is not more than 2.5 seconds when the overlap ratio becomes 0 per cent.
condition: if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary

text: In false reaction Scenario 3 (guidance), the subject vehicle drives at 30 km/h (+0/-2 km/h) toward a curve of radius not more than 25 m at the outer side, decelerates to not less than 22 km/h at curve entry with TTC to the stationary object not more than 1.6 seconds, drives in the outer lane at a constant speed of not less than 21 km/h, and the TTC is not more than 1.1 second when the overlap ratio with the stationary vehicle becomes 0 per cent or the offset ratio to the stationary pedestrian target becomes -100 per cent.
condition: if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary

text: In false reaction Scenario 4 (guidance), the subject vehicle drives a straight road at 40 km/h (+0/-2 km/h) and begins to steer to change lane in front of the signboard with TTC to the signboard not more than 4.2 seconds, with no other vehicles approaching; during the lane change speed is constant and the TTC is not more than 3.3 seconds when the offset ratio to the centre of the signboard becomes -100 per cent.
condition: if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary

text: Credibility of the toolchain used for virtual testing shall be demonstrated by the vehicle manufacturer to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service, considering the criteria capability, accuracy, correctness, fit for purpose and usability.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The virtual testing toolchain shall reflect the vehicle, system and components that are to be tested.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall provide to the Technical Service a description of the models and tools which constitute the toolchain and the method used to trace input data, parameters and output data back to the corresponding toolchain version.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall provide to the Technical Service the processes which ensure that personnel developing, testing and validating the toolchain have appropriate experience, expertise and training, and evidence that these processes are implemented and effective.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: For toolchain activities not directly controlled by the manufacturer, an explanation of measures taken to ensure confidence in the quality and integrity of these activities shall be provided.
condition: if any activities are not directly controlled by the manufacturer

text: The manufacturer shall provide a description of the input parameters, with any uncertainties in the model parameters, used to validate the models in the tools and toolchain.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall provide documentation demonstrating that the data used to validate the models covers the intended scope and functionality of the toolchain.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall provide a description of the overall approach to data management for the toolchain.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall provide a description of the management activities describing modifications between toolchain releases, version control and the review processes ensuring those modifications result in a toolchain that is still suitable.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: All parts of the toolchain, tools and models shall be described by the manufacturer.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The vehicle manufacturer shall define the validity domain of the toolchain and how it has been derived, including any AEBS performance influencing factors, parameter ranges, assumptions, limitations and tolerances.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The toolchain documentation shall include a description of the key performance indicators assessed during validation, such as time to collision, remaining distance or impact speed.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The toolchain documentation shall include a description of the accuracy requirements for the toolchain and its components, including comparison with physical tests.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The toolchain documentation shall include assumptions, limitations, uncertainties and the necessary levels of fidelity.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall provide a description of the toolchain assessment methodology, including the impact of any errors and uncertainties on the results and the consequences for compliance of the system with this Regulation.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall review the information produced in defining the validity domain (paragraph 2.3.6.2.) and document any implications for the use of the toolchain.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The toolchain and its components shall be capable of accurately representing the relevant aspects of the physical AEBS being modelled.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall provide documentation on the verification of the modelling implementing the AEBS function in the toolchain, including a description of the models, their implementation, how they represent the AEBS function and the activities performed to confirm correct implementation.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall provide an estimation of the numerical errors affecting the toolchain and its components and analysis that the errors remain sufficiently bounded.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall demonstrate the effect of variations of the model parameters on the output values, identify the most critical parameters influencing the results, and include a robust calibration procedure for these parameters.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The vehicle manufacturer shall describe the overall approach to toolchain validation including performance measures and a validation strategy, which shall be agreed by the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service, including physical tests demonstrating that the toolchain accurately represents the physical system.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The validation tests performed shall ensure a statistical comparison between physical and simulation results is possible.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The validation strategy shall be defined by the manufacturer and presented to the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service for review and agreement.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall demonstrate how the toolchain achieves the defined key performance indicators and accuracy requirements, including justification for their choice and the criteria for satisfying them.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall provide the list of validation scenarios and the parameter descriptions and accuracy requirements needed to perform the validation tests.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall provide documentation describing the validation performed to establish the credibility of the toolchain, including processes followed, physical tests performed and models and tools used.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The manufacturer shall provide documentation demonstrating how the uncertainty in the input data has been characterised and the model parameters evaluated.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The overall uncertainty of the virtual testing results shall be quantified based on the toolchain structure and the data flow through the toolchain, allowing estimates of likely errors and the required safety margins, which shall be applied to the results when the toolchain is used for virtual testing.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: At the request of the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service, additional confirmatory validation including physical tests shall be performed or witnessed.
condition: at the request of the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service

text: The number of physical validation tests shall be defined in agreement between the manufacturer and the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service and shall be sufficient to cover the validity domain specified by the vehicle manufacturer.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: The methodology used to generate physical validation data, such as data recording equipment, data processing and calculation of scalar values, shall be documented as part of the validation documentation.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: Compliance of the AEBS with the performance requirements of paragraphs 5.2.1 to 5.2.2. may be demonstrated by virtual testing of the dynamic manoeuvres of paragraphs 6.4. to 6.6. only using a toolchain meeting Annex 4.
condition: at the request of the vehicle manufacturer

text: All virtual testing results provided by the manufacturer in applying for an approval shall refer to the toolchain evaluated and validated according to this annex.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: For each approval application the manufacturer shall confirm that the virtual testing was conducted using a validated toolchain.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: For each approval application the manufacturer shall confirm that the virtual testing was performed by staff with appropriate competences and skills.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: For each approval application the manufacturer shall confirm that the virtual testing was performed using a toolchain with a unique identifier and sufficient information, including scope, regulatory applicability and validation history, to ensure traceability and assurance that the toolchain is suitable and fit for purpose.
condition: where virtual testing is used

text: For each approval application the manufacturer shall confirm that the virtual testing was performed using a toolchain within its scope and in accordance with any restrictions.
condition: where virtual testing is used
